owner: W1-TRIBES. The six peoples of RI-LOR08, disagreeing in front of the player.
note: Two kinds of topic live here and the difference is W1-23's ruling. Topics whose infos carry `cf` and `pos` are DISPUTES — a disagreement about what IS THE CASE — and `game/src/world/canon.js#allows` offers each line only to a speaker the register says holds that side. Topics with no `cf` at all are ARGUMENTS — a disagreement about what is WORTH DOING — and they are deliberately unregistered, because there is no fact underneath them to be right about. Registering an argument would flatter it. See RI-LOR08 §4.

infos.x: More than you'll meet. Mine are the Agacephs and we're four days into the Deep Marshes, which is four days if you go with one of us and never if you go alone. Who put you on to asking?

There's a number. It isn't a small one. My grandmother would point at the lights on the water at night and say that many, and she was not a woman who exaggerated about anything else. I have sat down with nine and I am not young.

I can tell you where the smoke is. Fourteen fires in the Stone Forest at the end of the dry, and a fire is a people or a piece of one. Is that a count? It's what I have and it's more than the man in the court building has.
Paatru. That's the whole answer and you can have it for nothing.
Paatru. Clay Moor. They have me down here as a river name because the clerk couldn't spell the other one and wouldn't ask.

There are peoples, and there are the estates, and the Office enters both in the same column. I've objected to that in writing twice and had a courteous letter back both times. Do you want the peoples or do you want the column?
Naga-Kur. Dead-Water in your mouth. We're north and you're not going north.

The Office recognises four native bodies. I've surveyed nine peoples in three years and the grant doesn't ask me to reconcile the two figures, so I haven't. Would you carry a letter for me if I wrote one?
You are asking a Miredancer about the count. We are the ones who will tell you the count is a foreign question and then give you a number anyway. Nine that I have eaten with. More that I have not.

Distance is nothing to a root. A man who dies at Tear is home by evening and the tree is no poorer for the journey. If that were false the Dres would pay the same for a corpse as for a working hand, and they don't. Have you a better account of the prices?

I've sent people out to Tear and I've sent people out to Blackrose and I have never once been shown a reason to think the tree loses them. My father died at sea. My father is under the grange. Both of those are true and I sleep.

The nearest root still listening takes what it can reach. It isn't his tree. He goes out again in a place he has never been and he comes out a stranger to the ones who made him, and the tree that did make him is short by one that year. Does that sound like coming home to you?

The pattern goes to whatever is nearest and awake. That's not cruelty, it's reach. A tree in the Rootlands is not going to hear a man die outside Tear any more than you'd hear a door shut in Gideon from here.

My grandfather went down on the coast. The ground where he fell got heavy and it's still heavy, and you can feel it through a boot. What came back to us came back short. I've never had a word for how short.
Distance costs. Ask any of us who has fetched a body and we'll all tell you the same, and none of us will tell you the rate. So carry them, if you can carry them.
We carry ours back. Every one, every time, and we have paid for it in the open. Ask the warders on this gate what the spring cost us.

The tree behind that wall is ours and it stood before the Office did. My great-grandmother's egg was under it. The wall is forty years old and it went up over theft, not over shame, and I'd have thought the difference obvious.
It's a Hist. It's entered on the survey as a Hist and it pays tithe as a Hist and no rootkeeper who has come to look has said otherwise to my face. Have you seen it? The gate's open before noon.
A cutting. A man carried it off the Rootlands in a wet sack and put it in a hole and built a wall round the hole. It grows. It drinks. It holds nothing.
Taste the water under it. Ours runs black and theirs runs clear, and clear means the root isn't going down, it's going sideways looking for something. Go and taste it before you take my word.

It is a true tree. That is the part Helstrom has wrong and the part the family will not hear from me. It is a true tree and it has stopped answering, and I would rather it were a cutting, because a cutting was never listening in the first place.
Real, and quiet. I've sat under it. You can tell a quiet tree from a dead stick the way you can tell a sleeping man from a chair.

Sap is sap. It comes off the same tree, it goes into the same hatchling, and the vessel is a vessel. My own name was given to me out of a copper cup in a room with a window and I have never once felt short of anything.
We bring it to them because the yard is safer than the root. Have you ever watched a hatching at a wild well? Half of them go into the water and a third of those don't come out.

The tree has to be there. Not the sap — the tree, over it, with the roots under it, and it must see. What comes out of a cup is a body with something borrowed in it, and the borrowing is called in at the end. I have been down four times and I would say this to any of them to their faces.
You wouldn't marry by letter. Same objection, same answer, and the Archein have been giving me the same shrug about it since I was small.
No. The tree looks at it or the tree does not. We've no argument beyond that one and we've never needed one.

They get a soul. And they come back short — the Court has the figures and the figures run four hundred years. Estate-hatched, cup-given: they die a little young and they bury a little heavy, and I've stopped saying so at Gideon because of what it does to a room.

One night. Every stepped ruin in the province has gone over the same way, north-east shoulder first, and you cannot see that from the ground and I have seen it from the air a hundred times. What knocks a whole country down in one direction? Weather doesn't do it over four hundred years.

Generations. We have the tablets — the Speakers kept them and the hand changes three times inside the falling, and a hand changes when a person dies. So it was long. It was long enough for three people to grow old writing it down.
Slow. The tablets are in the rootpost and I'll show them to you if you can be quiet for an hour. Three hands, and the last one is shaky.

Three burnings. Not one. The clay has three black seams in it and there is clean clay between them, and clay does not lie about that sort of thing. Dig a pit anywhere on the moor and you'll find them at the same depths.
Three. You want to argue it, bring a spade in the dry season and I'll stand over you while you dig.

I have four accounts and they contradict each other on the number of events, the century, and whether it was fire at all. The grant renews on findings. So I write what I can measure and I leave the rest to the next man with a grant.
This one is Ashu. She's on the shield because she asked to be, and she fights, and I have felt her turn the shield twice. You may think that's the strap. I was there for both.

The pattern left at the moment of death. A bone is a bone after that — good bone, honoured bone, still bone. The Court has never found anything in one and the Court has looked, professionally, for four hundred years.

It holds nothing and it delays the going. Both at once. So the warrior gets no company and the tree waits, and the one who waits was not asked and cannot be asked. That is what I would say to them if they came south, and they do not come south.
Nothing in the bone. A cost all the same, and the cost is paid at the other end by a hatchling nobody has met yet. I like the Naga-Kur. I have said this to them and they fed me anyway.

Roosts. They're a hand and a half wide at the top and they run between the high steps and they go nowhere a foot needs to go. And they're worn on the outside edge, where a claw sits. We were up there. Somebody built them for us and then went away.

Roads. They run door to door and they have kerbs, and a kerb is for keeping a load on. Nobody flew. My people have said this for as long as we've said anything and the Sarpa laugh at us from a branch.
Roads, and I'll tell you the tell. There are steps at both ends. Why would you build steps up to a roost?

Aqueducts. There's a fall of one part in four hundred along the whole run, which is too consistent to be an accident and far too shallow for a road. I've measured eight. I would like to measure eighty and I would like to do it without being shot at.

topics.name: what your people will not do

infos.x: I won't tell you the way. I'll take you and I'll bring you back, and at the end of it you still won't know the way. The Ledger has been trying to buy a chart off us for thirty years and they've had thirty years of dinners out of it.
We don't chase. If it has to be run down we don't eat it, and that's the weir there, and the weir is why we sit still so much. Are you hungry or are you just asking?
We don't cross another people's bridge. Ford or wait, and in the wet we wait, and in the wet we lose one or two waiting.
We don't take anyone in. Not you, not a Miredancer, not a hatchling off the coast with the right eyes. So don't ask twice, because the second ask is a different thing.
I don't come down into a place I haven't been asked into. I'll go round it for a day first. Thorn worked that out and put a mark on the roof, and now I come to Thorn.

I do not deal at the quay. Not with a Dres captain, not with his mate, not on his deck. A factor stands between and that is not a nicety, it is the entire distinction, and I will hear it argued for as long as you care to argue it.
We don't stop the Speaker drinking. Not for anything. There isn't a Miredancer alive who would put a hand on that cup, and I'd know, because I'm the one drinking out of it.
We don't leave a body. Not ever, not for weather, not for numbers. Three of us went back into the water at Keel last year and two came out.
We'll bury anybody's dead. Archein, Imperial, a Dres factor if he's brought to us. That one is not popular and it hasn't changed.

In the wet the clay holds the year's eggs. A stranger in it is there for the eggs, because for as long as we've counted, a stranger in it has been there for the eggs. So in the wet a stranger is killed and no one is asked about it afterwards. Do you want to know what the dry season is like, or have you heard enough?
You're standing in a market talking to me, so it's the dry. Come up in the rains and it's a different law and the same people. I don't apologise for it and I don't expect you to like it.
The Paatru have a season for it. That doesn't make it small if it's your season. I've lost two out of a party of six on the moor and both of them were mine to keep out of it.
It's a law. A bad one, and a law, and I would rather deal with a bad law than a temper. You always know where you are with the Paatru — you're in the wrong place, in the wrong month.

Four times. Four descents, and I have come back with nothing four times, and my mouth is gold and my arms have gone to bark. On the eighth day I go down again. What would you have me do instead — sit in the rootpost and be a decoration?

She'll go down. I've said what I have to say about it and she listened properly, which is worse than not listening. There isn't a rule about this. There's a woman and a hole and a lot of us standing round the top of it.
That's the Miredancers' business. If it were mine I would have taken the cup off her, and it isn't mine, and I've thought about it more than I'd like to.
A woman is poisoning herself in public for a tradition and the province calls it piety. I'd send a physician. They wouldn't let him past the post and I've stopped offering.

Yes, the labour goes out under lease and yes, some of it ends up on a Dres deck. It does not go from my hand to his hand. There's a factor in Gideon and the paper is his and the money comes back through him, and if you cannot see the difference I can't put it any plainer.
Ask what my grandfather did and you'll get the quay, and the deck, and the shouting. Ask what I do and you get a letter. That is two generations of work and I'd like it noticed.
He says there's a man in the middle. There's a man in the middle. And the one at the far end is on a ship either way, so I don't know what the man in the middle is for except him.
They took me at the trade-edge in the dry. The clerk wrote down that I came voluntarily to a place of trade, and that is a true sentence, and it is not what happened.
I've heard him make that case at a table and make it well. It's a real distinction. It's a real distinction about the paper.
A word for it. They've all got a word for it now. Ours is shorter.
The tracks north are shut and they'll stay shut, and after the tracks it's the road, and after the road it's Thorn. The Deep-Kin talk about this in a room. We started.

Not like this. To empty the coast you have to get to the coast, and getting anywhere in this province is us, and I have not agreed to that and I will not be asked politely for long. Do you know what it is to be the road?
They argue about it under a roof and I sit on the roof. When it's decided I'll hear the decision, and until then it's warm up there and the talking goes on a long time.
They count us in. No one has come up the moor to ask us and no one is going to, because of what happens to people who come up the moor. So we're in it, apparently.
We come. We sit. We don't vote. Everyone trusts us and nobody speaks for us, and I've decided I prefer that to the other arrangement.
